summary: Foundation models like GPT-4, Llama 3, Claude 3, and Gemini Ultra are pretrained on trillions of tokens and refined with RLHF, but hallucination and sycophancy remain unresolved alignment challenges. Retrieval-Augmented Generation, introduced by Lewis et al. in 2020, grounds LLM responses in external verifiable knowledge by encoding a document corpus into a shared embedding space and retrieving the top-k passages at inference time — significantly reducing hallucination without model retraining. This week's lab will implement a RAG pipeline using LangChain and ChromaDB; students must clone the repository and install dependencies before Thursday, read the Lewis et al. paper, and submit a team project proposal by Friday midnight. Evaluating RAG requires a multi-faceted toolkit: Recall at K, MRR, and NDCG for retrieval quality, and ROUGE, BERTScore, and RAGAS for generation quality — no single metric is sufficient.
action_items: Please clone the lab repository and install the dependencies listed in the requirements.txt file before Thursday's session.
